name: Elastic - Stuxbot Threat Hunt (KQL Queries)
description: Full Stuxbot threat hunt walkthrough using Kibana/Elastic. Covers every KQL query in the investigation chain: file download → execution → C2 → lateral movement. Data sources: windows* index (Sysmon, Windows Events, PowerShell logs) and zeek* index (network).
source: CDSA Module 04: Introduction to Threat Hunting & Hunting With Elastic
notes:
=== Lab Setup ===
Kibana: http://<TARGET_IP>:5601 → Discover
Set time range: Last 15 years
Set timezone: Management → Kibana Settings → Europe/Copenhagen

Index patterns:
  windows*   → Windows audit logs + Sysmon + PowerShell logs (~118,975 logs)
  zeek*      → Zeek network logs (~332,261 logs)

=== Hunt Chain (Stuxbot Phishing Campaign) ===

STEP 1 — Did the malicious OneNote file download? (Sysmon Event 15 = FileCreateStreamHash)
  event.code:15 AND file.name:*invoice.one
  → 3 hits → confirmed download

STEP 2 — Corroborate with file create + Zone Identifier (Sysmon Event 11)
  event.code:11 AND file.name:invoice.one*
  → Confirms download from internet (Zone.Identifier appended)
  → host.hostname field shows: WS001
  → source IP: 192.168.28.130 (confirmed via Event ID 3 query below)

  Confirm host IP via Sysmon Event 3:
  event.code:3 AND host.hostname:WS001   → check source.ip field

STEP 3 — DNS queries from infected host around download time (Zeek logs)
  source.ip:192.168.28.130 AND dns.question.name:*
  Add columns: dns.question.name
  Filter out noise: NOT (google.com OR google-analytics.com OR ...)
  → Look for unusual domains → found file.io, suspicious ad domains
  → C2 IPs identified: 34.197.10.85, 3.213.216.16

STEP 4 — Did invoice.one get opened? (Sysmon Event 1)
  event.code:1 AND process.command_line:*invoice.one*
  → 1 hit: ONENOTE.EXE opened invoice.one 6 seconds after download

STEP 5 — Child processes of OneNote (Sysmon Event 1)
  event.code:1 AND process.parent.name:"ONENOTE.EXE"
  → cmd.exe executing invoice.bat from temp directory

STEP 6 — Child processes of the batch file
  event.code:1 AND process.parent.command_line:*invoice.bat*
  → powershell.exe downloading content from Pastebin (C2 stager)
  → Note process.pid for next step (e.g. 9944)

STEP 7 — All activity from the PowerShell process by PID
  process.pid:"9944" AND process.name:"powershell.exe"
  Add columns: event.code, file.path, dns.question.name, destination.ip
  → File creation (default.exe dropped to disk)
  → DNS: ngrok.io → C2 IP 18.158.249.75
  → Connections to DC1 (lateral movement prep)

STEP 8 — Did the dropped executable run? (process name search)
  process.name:"default.exe"
  → 68 hits: DNS queries for ngrok, C2 connections, dropped SharpHound.exe + svchost.exe
  → Parent process on PKI server: PSEXESVC.exe → confirms PSExec lateral movement
  → user.name: svc-sql1 → confirms account compromise

STEP 9 — Did SharpHound (AD recon) execute?
  process.name:"SharpHound.exe"
  → 4 hits: executed twice with collection method 'all'

STEP 10 — Is the malware hash present on other hosts? (IOC hunt)
  process.hash.sha256:018d37cbd3878258c29db3bc3f2988b6ae688843801b9abc28e6151141ab66d4
  → 12 hits: WS001 and PKI server both infected
  Add column: host.hostname to identify all compromised systems

STEP 11 — How was svc-sql1 compromised? (lateral logon audit)
  (event.code:4624 OR event.code:4625) AND winlog.event_data.LogonType:3 AND source.ip:192.168.28.130
  → Failed logons for administrator (password spray attempt)
  → Successful logons for svc-sql1 on PKI and PAW (credential compromise confirmed)

=== Key IOCs (Stuxbot) ===
  File:     invoice.one
  Batch:    invoice.bat (temp directory)
  Malware:  default.exe, svchost.exe (fake), payload.exe, VBS file
  Recon:    SharpHound.exe (C:\Users\Public\)
  C2:       ngrok.io → 18.158.249.75, 3.125.102.39
  C2 IPs:   34.197.10.85, 3.213.216.16
  SHA256:   018d37cbd3878258c29db3bc3f2988b6ae688843801b9abc28e6151141ab66d4
  User:     svc-sql1 (compromised)
  Hosts:    WS001 (initial), PKI (lateral via PSExec)
  Lateral:  PSEXESVC.exe (PSExec), PowerShell Remoting (WinRM)
